subject.title: Feature: Telegram Reactions - Two-Way Support with Prompt Guidance

question: Should OpenClaw add a distinct Telegram `reactionGuidance` configuration surface for interpreting incoming reactions, or keep reaction behavior governed solely by the existing reaction-level and notification controls?
rationale: The requested behavior is a new user-facing policy and config surface whose relationship to existing reaction settings, default prompt behavior, and passive versus turn-triggering semantics cannot be resolved safely from source alone.

options.title: Keep the existing controls
options.body: Reject a separate guidance setting and clarify/document how existing notification and reaction-level behavior should be interpreted.

options.title: Add a distinct opt-in policy
options.body: Define a Telegram-owned guidance contract with explicit `off|minimal|full` semantics, notification gating, upgrade behavior, and focused configuration coverage.

options.title: Fold it into reaction-trigger work
options.body: Defer incoming-reaction interpretation until maintainers choose the broader cross-channel reaction-input model tracked by the related reaction-trigger requests.

recommendation.title: Keep the existing controls
recommendation.body: Reject a separate guidance setting and clarify/document how existing notification and reaction-level behavior should be interpreted.

likelyOwner.reason: The current reaction configuration and prompt-adapter behavior traces back to this feature-history owner.
